selectedOriginals.sourceFamily: commons:miami freedom tower by tom schaefer 2.jpg
selectedOriginals.inspection: Full selected front detail inspected: pale yellow rough stucco and pale cast-stone quoined piers; elaborate central round portal with layered archivolts, raised paired columns/Corinthian-like capitals, scroll broken pediment/central cartouche and two small seated figures. Upper arched glazed balcony door/iron rail and two actual quatrefoil windows; great sweeping curved cornice rises to a small central top window/scrolled pediment. Tall rectangular upper-shaft windows in three columns. Exact sculpture and inscriptions simplified as original geometric ornament.

selectedOriginals.caption: Freedom Tower in a cloudy and rainy night
selectedOriginals.inspection: Full selected2011night view inspected: nine plain three-column shaft window rows with corner quoins, decorated square crown/setback open lantern/copper cap/vane. Red colored floodlighting is not baked into materials. Night/event structures/traffic/street furniture omitted.

additionalInspected.caption: A southeast view of Freedom Tower, Miami, Florida
additionalInspected.inspection: Full2016SE original inspected: east front centered beneath tower, long plain south printing wing extending west. Basement openings, tall divided hall casements and upper casements; stone window frames, shallow open balustraded balconies and front raised entrance stair/terrace. Native photos show three column tower rhythm, major bracketed cornices, corner open turrets, square ornamental crown and tall upper lantern. No neighboring college buildings/plaza/palms/banner surfaces.

additionalInspected.caption: Top of the Freedom Tower, Downtown Miami, Florida. The building commemorates Cuban immigration and nowadays houses, among other facilities, a museum.
additionalInspected.inspection: Full2018NE crown original inspected: large projecting bracketed cornice and balustrade at lower square stage; four small corner turrets with real arched openings/green pyramidal caps/metal finials. Upper square has central arched glazed light, flanking rectangular lights, blind roundels and cartouche/foliate frames. Crown parapet has real turned-baluster counters and obelisks. Octagonal upper drum alternates arched dark openings and blind faces/oculi, engaged columns/capitals/brackets; upper balcony/small drum/copper dome, small open copper beacon and ship vane.

additionalInspected.caption: Freedom Tower
additionalInspected.inspection: Full2012portal detail inspected: actual semicircular deep portal, oak paneled double leaves shown open, ornate fanlight/iron radial counter pattern, paired stone columns and large scrolled pediment/cartouche. Arched balcony door above, open iron balcony rail and side quatrefoil glazing are real depth features. Model uses closed oak leaves as a fixed exterior state and original simplified cartouche/foliate/figures.

additionalInspected.caption: U.S. National Register of Historic Places
additionalInspected.inspection: Full2017SWoriginal inspected: south plain side/cast-stone east facade relationship and raised front stair/low terrace. Confirms white/pale stone versus warm yellow fields, many small obelisks across roof edge/corner groups, full height three-column plain shaft, ornate square stage, tall drum and green dome/ship vane. Construction crane/traffic lamps/banner letters/statue and neighboring campus omitted.

sources.inspection: NPS heritage page read:1925 Schultze&Weaver newspaper building, Mediterranean/Spanish and Italian vocabulary, Giralda-derived tower, oak doors/iron transom/balconies/cast ornament. Historic character corroborates local exterior photographs; not used as a current2026finish survey.

2008 NHL nomination: read complete relevant pages4,5,8 and inspected rendered pages. East-facing entrance;125ft is property frontage, not a substitute footprint. Basement/lobby about3ft above grade; rear printing wing is relatively plain. Plain tower has corner quoins and three bays; setback crown/balustrades lead to cupola. Restored copper weather vane is19ft tall. Interior rooms and literal sculptural replicas excluded.
